title: Lint a workflow before it can run

blocks.text: The vegetation team is writing its own CI workflow for the trim planner. Before any workflow in the organisation may run, a lint step reads it, parsed by PyYAML, and refuses the habits this lesson warns about.

In `workflow_lint.py`, write `lint(workflow)`. `workflow` is the parsed file (a dict; remember that PyYAML reads the key `on` as `True`, which this check does not need). Return the sorted findings, each once, as these exact texts:

items: `workflow: no top-level permissions` when the workflow has no `permissions` key, and `workflow: permissions write-all` when it is the string `write-all`. A job whose `permissions` is `write-all` gives `JOB: permissions write-all`.

`JOB: REF is not pinned to a commit SHA` for every `uses:` value not of the form `owner/name@` followed by a full 40-character lower-case hex SHA. A local action, whose `uses` starts with `./`, is code in the same repository and needs no pin.
`JOB: uses secret NAME` for every `secrets.NAME` found anywhere in a job's steps (`run`, `with`, `env`, at any depth), except `GITHUB_TOKEN`, the token GitHub gives every job.

`JOB: id-token: write without an AWS credentials step` when a job's permissions grant `id-token: write` and none of its steps uses `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials`. A job with no `permissions` key of its own gets the workflow's, so a workflow-level `id-token: write` counts for it; a job that sets its own `permissions` uses only those. (The `write-all` finding, above, looks only at what each level writes itself.)

blocks.text: `PINNED`, `SECRET`, `AWS_STEP` and `texts` (every string inside a value) are given; about 20 lines remain.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
from workflow_lint import lint

SHA = "a" * 40
flow = {
    "name": "depot-ci",
    "permissions": {"contents": "read", "id-token": "write"},
    "jobs": {
        "check": {"runs-on": "ubuntu-24.04", "steps": [
            {"uses": "actions/setup-python@v6"},
            {"uses": "./.github/actions/prepare"},
            {"run": "echo ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} && make test"}]},
        "ship": {"runs-on": "ubuntu-24.04", "permissions": "write-all", "steps": [
            {"uses": f"actions/checkout@{SHA}"},
            {"run": "deploy", "env": {"TOKEN": "${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}"}}]},
    },
}

findings = lint(flow)
print("depot-ci findings:", len(findings))
for finding in findings:
    print("  ", finding)

cases.says: a clean workflow has no findings; one with a tag, a stored key and no permissions has three
a seven-character SHA is not a pin, and a local ./ action needs none
write-all permissions are found on the workflow and on a job
a secret inside a run line is found; GITHUB_TOKEN is allowed
a job that may request an OIDC token but never uses it is caught
a job with no permissions of its own inherits the workflow's id-token: write, and is caught the same way
